title: Regional guardrails and automated degradation triggers for tier-aware routing
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: We need a lightweight, deterministic system to automatically degrade requests to lower-cost/compatible model variants or alternate regions when regional capacity, elevated 429s, or timeouts threaten customer SLAs. This ticket designs and implements regional guardrails and automated degradation triggers that are tier-aware (tier routing) and avoid noisy cascades across regions. Goal: provide clear, testable triggers for automatic fallback, a throttle window to prevent flapping, and observability hooks for post-incident analysis. Scope: trigger types (rate-limit 429 spikes, tail latency/timeouts, sustained error-rate), per-tenant tier policies, regional impact isolation, cooldown/backoff policy, metrics and dashboards, and a canary rollout for internal traffic before customer rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Defined trigger thresholds for 429 spikes, request timeouts, and 5xx error-rate with example defaults and tenant override rules
Implementation of a region-aware degrader that can: mark a route as degraded, re-route to fallback model variant or alternate region, and emit structured events to trace requests
Circuit protection: per-region and per-tenant soft/hard limits to avoid cross-region cascading failures
Cooldown/backoff logic that enforces progressive backfills (e.g., gradual traffic reintroduction) and inhibits rapid flapping
End-to-end tests covering synthetic 429 spike, injected timeout, and sustained error scenarios
Dashboard panels for signal surface (429 rate, p95/p99 latency, rollback events) and alerting rules tied to degradation actions
Canary rollout gated behind feature flag and internal traffic experiment (>=2 days of stable metrics)
implementation_steps: Design: finalize thresholds and policy model (regional vs global, soft vs hard limits) and document in design doc
Runtime: add degrader component to router that observes signal streams and evaluates policy rules per-route and per-region
Fallbacks: wire in model-variant mapping so routing can select compatible lower-cost/quantized variants or alternate regions
Circuit protection: add token-bucket/backpressure layer preventing too many degrade actions per minute per-region
Observability: emit structured events (degrade_start, degrade_end, degrade_rollback) with metadata and attach trace IDs
Testing: unit tests, integration tests with local failure injection, and chaos test in staging cluster
Rollout: feature-flagged canary -> gradual ramp -> full rollout with metrics monitor
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluation logic across combinations of signals
Integration test that simulates 429 spike in us-east-1 and verifies degrade event, re-route to fallback, and cooldown behavior
Chaos engineering run that kills 2/3 routers in a region to validate non-cascading behavior
Customer simulation: replay production traces with injected 10% timeout to verify SLA preservation and cost impact
Post-canary verification: 48-hour pulse check for error-rate, latency, and cost delta
metrics_targets: no more than 2% uplift in median latency for fallbacks
customer-facing 99th percentile latency preserved within SLA 95% of the time during events
rollout should not increase global 5xx rate by >0.2%
rollback_plan: Feature-flag toggle to disable automatic degradation immediately
Manual evacuation of degrade state for affected routes via admin API
Automated rollback window: if post-rollout metrics breach safety thresholds for >10m, abort ramp and revert flag
Postmortem and adjustments to thresholds before reattempt

notes: Tradeoffs: aggressive defaults reduce customer impact but increase fallback cost. We will expose tenant-level override with billing guardrails.
Edge cases: cross-region network partitions where the router sees false high 429 counts; mitigated by requiring sustained windows and cross-checks with regional health API.
Future: integrate with Optimize to recommend fallback model variants based on quantization/cost profiles per workload.
